rows.q: How many party slots are open at the start of the Heart of Sinnoh campaign?
rows.a: Three. One more slot opens each time you gain the Shard of Emotion, Knowledge or Willpower. Shards do not increase your Movement. The Ultra Burst campaign starts with all 6 slots open.

rows.q: Who picks their home village first?
rows.a: The game picks the first player at random, and the choice then goes round anticlockwise. The last player to pick takes the first turn.

rows.q: Are Starter Pokémon and Trainer Cards picked in turn order?
rows.a: No. Everyone picks at the same time, and the picks are revealed together once all players have chosen.

rows.q: Can I pick the Ultra Megalopolis as my home village?
rows.a: Only in the Ultra Burst campaign.

rows.q: Where does a Starter Pokémon's card go when I release it?
rows.a: To the discard pile of the Weak Pokémon deck. The Starter Pokémon nobody picked are also shuffled into the Weak Pokémon deck at the start of the game.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: How do I count a difference of "2 or more full elevations"? What about forests and lakes?
rows.a: Only the pillars stacked on a tile count as elevations. A forest's canopy and a lake's water do not count, so Plains and Forest are both elevation 1, and Ocean and lakes are elevation 0.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: Does Fly need an Apricorn of a particular colour?
rows.a: No. Any 1 Apricorn will do, whatever its colour or tier.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: Can I make both trades on a Ginkgo Trade card in one turn?
rows.a: Yes. You may make just one or both, but each trade only once.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: Can I pay for one Ginkgo trade with the Apricorns I received from the other?
rows.a: Yes. You may make the two trades in either order and spend the Apricorns from the first on the second.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: Which colour of Apricorn do I get when a wild Pokémon flees at a mixed-colour Apricorn Reef?
rows.a: You choose the colours yourself, up to the number you gain (Weak 2 · Moderate 1 · Strong 0).

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: How many times per turn can I make a Stew? What about village actions?
rows.a: Each kind of Stew can be made once per turn. Each village action can be used once per turn, and you may use several different ones in the same turn.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: Can I still Search, pick up Apricorns or reveal a Hidden Spot on a tile where I have run out of Movement?
rows.a: Yes. Anything you do on the tile you are standing on works even with 0 Movement left. If your last step takes you onto an Apricorn Tree, you can Search it that same turn.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: Does my turn end automatically when I run out of Movement?
rows.a: No. Your turn only ends when you choose End Turn, have a battle, or pick up Apricorns after a Search that found no Pokémon.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: Do village actions (Heal · Ginkgo Merchants trade · Fly) need Movement left over?
rows.a: No. Village actions do not depend on Movement, and Fly does not spend any.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: If I visit both a village and a campsite in one turn, can I Heal twice?
rows.a: No. Each village action is once per turn across villages, campsites and the Ultra Megalopolis combined.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: Do I have to take the shortest route when I move?
rows.a: No. As long as you have the Movement, you may take a detour and even step on a tile you have already passed. Each tile costs 1 Movement.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: What happens when I pass over a Hidden Spot while walking?
rows.a: You stop on that tile and are asked whether to reveal it. If you choose Pass, you carry on along your chosen route, and you must come back to that tile to reveal it later.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: What happens to the rest of my move if I reveal a Hidden Spot partway through?
rows.a: The rest of your chosen route is cancelled and you stay on that tile. Once the result is resolved, you can move again with your remaining Movement (if a battle took place, your turn ends).

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: What if a Search finds fewer matching Pokémon than it should draw?
rows.a: Only the matching Pokémon appear. If none appear at all, your turn continues with no encounter.

rows.sectionTitle: Movement · Things You Do on the Board
rows.q: My Search found nothing. Can I Search the same tile again this turn?
rows.a: No. You cannot Search the same tile twice in one turn.

rows.q: Do I have to reveal a Hidden Spot when I pass over it?
rows.a: No. Revealing it is your choice. Once it is revealed, though, its effect must be resolved, and if an Alpha Pokémon appears you cannot avoid the battle.

rows.q: Can I use a Zesty Stew after an Alpha Pokémon has appeared?
rows.a: No. You have to use it before revealing the Hidden Spot. On the turn you use it, Alpha Pokémon will not battle you, and the token stays face-up on its tile.

rows.q: Must I fight when I enter a tile with a face-up Alpha token?
rows.a: No. The battle is only forced at the moment the token is revealed.

rows.q: How do I battle an Alpha Pokémon that was left face-up?
rows.a: Search on that tile, and the same Alpha battle starts as when a Hidden Spot is revealed.

rows.q: Does an Alpha Pokémon always attack first?
rows.a: No. The side with the higher Initiative goes first. An Alpha Pokémon starts with the Initiative Advantage token, so it only attacks first when Initiative is tied.

rows.q: What do I gain for capturing or defeating an Alpha Pokémon?
rows.a: You gain 4 Journey Points, as for a Legendary Pokémon; if you defeated it, you gain 2 more and may teach its move. It is not an Apricorn Tree or Reef, so you gain no Apricorns.

rows.q: Does capturing an Alpha Pokémon earn the "Capture a Legendary" Journey Stamp?
rows.a: Yes, it does.

rows.q: Can a captured Alpha Pokémon hold a held item?
rows.a: No. The Alpha token permanently occupies its held item slot and cannot be removed.

rows.q: What happens to the token if I lose to an Alpha Pokémon or forfeit?
rows.a: The token is discarded and does not stay on the board. Even if you lose by forfeiting, you do not return to your home village as long as you still have a Pokémon able to battle.

rows.q: Does an Artifact give +1 attack strength just by being in my bag?
rows.a: No. A Pokémon has to be holding it, and it only applies to that Pokémon's moves of the two types shown on the Artifact. You can attach or remove an Artifact at any time outside of battle.

rows.q: Does the Artifact needed to meet a Legendary Pokémon also have to be held by a Pokémon?
rows.a: No. It can be in your bag or held by a Pokémon. You do not lose the Artifact when you meet the Legendary Pokémon.

rows.q: Can a fainted Pokémon evolve?
rows.a: Yes. Evolving fully restores a Pokémon first, so a fainted Pokémon is restored as it evolves.

rows.q: If the card I would evolve into is no longer in the Evolution Pokémon deck, am I unable to evolve?
rows.a: You can still evolve. The evolution goes ahead even when the card is not in the deck.

rows.q: Is the Infused Stew's half-price evolution automatically used on my first evolution of the turn?
rows.a: No. You choose which of that turn's evolutions to use it on. If you do not use it, it is lost at the end of the turn.

rows.q: Can I teach, replace or forget moves during a battle?
rows.a: Yes, but not while your own Pokémon's attack is being resolved (from rolling the dice until the damage is applied).

rows.q: Can a move gained as a Journey Stamp reward be taught to any Pokémon?
rows.a: No. Like any other move, it can only be taught to a Pokémon that can learn moves of that type.

rows.q: Can I move held items around during another player's turn?
rows.a: Yes. You can move them on another player's turn as long as you are not in a battle.

rows.q: Can I release a Pokémon during a battle?
rows.a: No. You cannot release Pokémon while any battle is in progress, whether it is yours or another player's. The only exception is when you have no room for a Pokémon you have just captured.

rows.q: Can I release a Pokémon while I am picking an encounter or before I answer a Challenge?
rows.a: No. You cannot release Pokémon until you have answered a choice that leads into a battle. After you answer, you can release again.

rows.q: What happens to everything a Pokémon has when I release it?
rows.a: The Pokémon card goes to the discard pile of its original deck, and its moves are discarded. Held items return to your bag, but an Alpha Pokémon token is discarded with it.

rows.q: Can I re-teach a Journey Stamp move that was replaced by another move or forgotten?
rows.a: No. A move that is replaced or forgotten is discarded and does not come back.

rows.q: If I capture a Pokémon with a full party, can I release the one I just caught?
rows.a: Yes. You pick 1 Pokémon to release from among the new capture and the Pokémon in your party.

rows.q: Does a Pokémon I capture mid-battle keep its battle fatigue?
rows.a: No. A captured Pokémon has left the battle, so its battle fatigue resets to 0.

rows.q: How is a capture roll resolved?
rows.a: By the total of the dice rolled. Status symbols count as 0, regular hits as 1 and critical hits as 2; the capture succeeds if the total is equal to or greater than the Capture Rate.

rows.q: If the opposing Pokémon has a status effect, do all the status symbols in my capture roll become regular hits?
rows.a: No. Only 1 symbol becomes 1 regular hit.

rows.q: Does a capture roll add battle fatigue too?
rows.a: Yes. Battle fatigue goes up by 1 every time you roll the dice, whether to attack or to capture, and a fatigued Pokémon takes 3 damage from a capture roll as well.

rows.q: How much battle fatigue does a move that attacks twice in one turn add?
rows.a: It goes up by 1 for each roll.

rows.q: Can I throw a Poké Ball as soon as a battle starts?
rows.a: You can only throw a Poké Ball on your own turn. In a battle where the opponent acts first, you have to wait until your turn comes.

rows.q: A wild Pokémon fainted on the same turn it made my Pokémon faint. Does that count as it fleeing?
rows.a: No. The wild Pokémon fainted, so you win and gain every reward.

rows.q: The Pokémon the wild Pokémon made faint was my last one. Does it still count as fleeing?
rows.a: Yes. Weak, Moderate and Strong wild Pokémon flee, so you gain the Apricorns for a fled Pokémon and then return to your home village.

rows.q: Do Alpha Pokémon and Pokémon swarms also flee after making 1 of my Pokémon faint?
rows.a: No. Like Legendary Pokémon, they only flee after making all your Pokémon faint.

rows.q: Do I gain Apricorns or Journey Points if I forfeit a wild battle?
rows.a: No. The wild Pokémon returns to its deck and you gain nothing.

rows.q: If one of my Pokémon had already fainted before the battle, can I forfeit as soon as the battle starts?
rows.a: No. You can forfeit only after 1 of your Pokémon has fainted during that battle. Fainting from battle fatigue damage counts too.

rows.q: If initiative changes during a battle, is the turn order worked out again?
rows.a: No. Turn order is only worked out again when a Pokémon faints and a new one comes in. Switching moves and Paralysed do not change it.

rows.q: In a trainer battle, if only one side's Pokémon faints, who decides their next action first?
rows.a: The side whose Pokémon did not faint decides first whether to switch out, and then the side whose Pokémon fainted sends in their next Pokémon.

rows.q: Several effects happen at once and the order changes the outcome. Who decides the order?
rows.a: Effects are resolved simultaneously by default; when the order matters, the attacking side decides.

rows.q: When is battle fatigue damage applied?
rows.a: At the same time as that turn's attack damage and healing.

rows.q: When several effects change damage, in what order are they calculated?
rows.a: Take the dice roll result, add move and item effects and type effectiveness, apply any double damage effects, and then apply effects that reduce the total damage dealt, such as Burned or Prism Armour. Damage cannot go below 0.

rows.q: When is an effect like "take no damage from attacks that would only deal 2 or less damage" (Evasive Manoeuvres) checked?
rows.a: Against the value left after all damage-reducing effects have been applied.

rows.q: When is an effect that caps the damage taken applied?
rows.a: Last of all, after every other calculation is finished.

rows.q: Does an effect that increases positive type effectiveness damage (Weakness Analysis) also get multiplied by double damage effects?
rows.a: Yes. It is added to the type effectiveness damage first, so it is doubled along with everything else.

rows.q: Is an initiative tie judged by the value printed on the card or by the value after effects?
rows.a: By initiative after all effects such as Paralysed, held items and trainer cards. If those values are tied, the Initiative Advantage token can be used.

rows.q: Can battle fatigue damage make my Pokémon and the opponent faint together?
rows.a: Yes. Battle fatigue damage is applied at the same time as that roll's attack damage, so both Pokémon can faint together. The same goes for capture rolls.

rows.q: In a battle against a wild Pokémon or Team Galactic, if both Pokémon faint at the same time, who sends in their next Pokémon first?
rows.a: The same as in a trainer battle: the side holding the Initiative Advantage token sends in first.

rows.q: What happens when an effect has no valid target (no Pokémon of that type left in the deck, or the legendary Pokémon to find is already in another player's party)?
rows.a: The effect is skipped and nothing happens. If the effect has a limited number of uses, no use is spent either.

rows.q: If several players can respond at the same moment with Change of Fate or an ability, in what order are the responses resolved?
rows.a: Every player who can respond is asked at the same time, and the responses are applied in this order: the attacking side → the opposing side → players outside the battle (clockwise, starting from the player whose turn it is). A response that can no longer be used because of an earlier one is cancelled, and its card or use is not spent.

rows.q: Can I respond after seeing another player's response?
rows.a: Yes. Whenever someone responds, every player who can respond is asked once more. This repeats until nobody responds.

rows.q: My opponent used Dialga's reroll to make me roll my attack again. Can I answer with an ability that affects my roll?
rows.a: Yes. If you have not yet used the Psychic's Subtle Manipulation or the Guitarist's Amp die on that attack, you can use it on the rerolled result.

rows.q: Several effects change dice faces and the order changes the outcome. Who decides the order?
rows.a: The attacking side chooses the order when it changes the damage or whether a Pokémon faints. If the outcome is the same, you are not asked.

rows.q: Does a condition like "if the target is already Burned, this move deals double damage" count a status inflicted by this same attack?
rows.a: No. Such conditions look at the state before this attack's effects are resolved. For example, Mystical Fire only deals double damage to a target that was already Burned before the attack.

rows.q: For effects like "if any status symbols are rolled" or "for each critical hit", which dice are counted?
rows.a: The final result, after every effect that replaces or rerolls dice has finished.

rows.q: What happens when an effect that "increases attack strength to n" is combined with other attack strength modifiers?
rows.a: The move's attack strength is set to n first, and then the other modifiers (such as +2 against a Frozen target) are added.

rows.q: How long does the Paralysed effect "remove all regular hits from your very next attack" last?
rows.a: It only applies when that Pokémon attacks on its very next turn after becoming Paralysed. If it threw a ball that turn, or left play before then by switching out, fainting or the battle ending, this part is lost and only the −3 initiative remains.

rows.q: If a Pokémon became Paralysed while on the Bench or outside a battle, are its regular hits removed when it comes in and attacks later?
rows.a: No. Regular hits are only removed from the attack right after becoming Paralysed, so a later attack is not affected.

rows.q: Are regular hits also removed from a capture roll when a Paralysed Pokémon throws a ball?
rows.a: No. Paralysed only affects attacks, and a capture roll is not an attack.

rows.q: If Paralysed lowers initiative during a battle, is the turn order worked out again right away?
rows.a: No. The lowered initiative is used from the next time turn order is compared.

rows.q: If the attacking Pokémon and the attacked Pokémon are both Drowsy, how do the dice change?
rows.a: If the roll has only 1 regular hit, the two effects cancel out and it stays a regular hit. If it has 2 or more, one becomes a status symbol and one becomes a critical hit.

rows.q: When a Paralysed Pokémon attacks a Drowsy target, which is applied first, Paralysed or Drowsy?
rows.a: When dice-changing effects conflict, the attacking side decides the order. The default order is Drowsy first: 1 regular hit becomes a critical hit, and then the remaining regular hits are removed.

rows.q: When do I get to choose that order?
rows.a: In this game, the attacking player is only asked when the order changes the damage or whether a Pokémon faints; otherwise the default order is used. Wild Pokémon and Team Galactic are never asked when they attack.

rows.q: How is "the same move as last turn" judged for Confused?
rows.a: It is compared with the move that Pokémon used on its own previous turn. If it threw a ball that turn, or left play by switching out or the battle ending, it counts as having no previous move.

rows.q: Do I take Poisoned damage on the turn the battle ends?
rows.a: No. If the capture succeeded or the battle ended that turn, end-of-turn effects do not happen.

rows.q: A Poisoned Pokémon cannot heal, so what about a village's full heal or a move that also heals status effects (Heal Bell)?
rows.a: The status effects are removed first, so the healing works normally.

rows.q: Does a Frozen wild Pokémon still flee when it knocks out my Pokémon?
rows.a: No. A Frozen Pokémon cannot flee, so the battle continues. If all of your usable Pokémon faint, the battle ends without a reward.

rows.q: Can I forfeit while my Pokémon is Frozen?
rows.a: Yes. Forfeiting is neither switching out nor fleeing, so you can still do it once 1 of your Pokémon has fainted in this battle. The same is true under a move effect that prevents switching out or fleeing (Magma Storm, Sand Tomb and so on).

rows.q: Does a "when the target is next attacked" effect apply to the very attack that set it up?
rows.a: No. It applies once to the first attack after the current one ends, and then it is gone. It counts as used even if that attack deals 0 damage.

rows.q: Are "when the user next attacks" or "when the user is next attacked" effects used up on a turn when a ball is thrown?
rows.a: No. Throwing a ball is not an attack, so the effect is not used and stays in place.

rows.q: If a Pokémon with a "when the user next attacks" effect switches out, does the effect apply when it comes back in later?
rows.a: No. When a Pokémon leaves play by switching out, fainting, being captured or the battle ending, all of its "until the user switches out" effects and one-off "next …" effects are lost.

rows.q: If a limited effect (once per turn, once per battle and so on) does nothing because its condition was not met, is the use spent?
rows.a: No. If the condition was not met, there was no target, or you chose not to use it, the use is not spent.

rows.q: Do wild Pokémon and Team Galactic use optional effects worded with "may"?
rows.a: In this game they always use them, without being asked.

rows.q: Are regular hits added by an effect that adds dice faces to the next attack (Bulk Up and so on) also removed by Paralysed?
rows.a: Yes. The added faces are part of that roll, so Paralysed removes them too.

rows.q: When do moves that heal at the end of the turn (Moonlight, Repairing Rock, Power Plant) start healing?
rows.a: From the end of the turn on which the move was used.

rows.q: Does the same effect stack if it is applied more than once? What about different moves with identically worded effects?
rows.a: It does not stack. Even from different moves, identically worded effects only apply once (using both Moonlight and Repairing Rock still heals only 2 at the end of the turn).

rows.q: When Tempered Steel makes the user immune to status effects, what happens to a status effect it already has?
rows.a: The user's own status effects are removed first when the move is used.

rows.q: Do moves that prevent switching out or fleeing (Magma Storm, Sand Tomb and so on) still work if the target already has a status effect and so the status is not inflicted?
rows.a: Yes. The switch out and flee restriction is applied separately from the status effect.

rows.q: If a Pokémon under Frigid Ice is hit by an attack that deals 0 damage, does the attacker still become Frozen?
rows.a: Yes. It was still attacked even though the damage was 0, so the effect happens.

rows.q: Do effects extended to "until the end of the battle" by Eternal Glade end when that Pokémon switches out or faints?
rows.a: No. The extended effects apply to your whole party and carry over to the next Pokémon that comes in. This includes effects that heal at the end of the turn.

rows.q: What happens when a move that inflicts two status effects at once is used on a target that already has a status effect?
rows.a: Neither is inflicted.

rows.q: What happens to a Pokémon with two status effects?
rows.a: It suffers the effects of both. Only one of them counts towards a capture roll, though.

rows.q: If the target is immune to only one of two status effects inflicted at once, is the other one inflicted?
rows.a: Yes. Immunity is checked separately for each status effect.

rows.q: How is the status effect inflicted by Splash, Tri Attack or Power Gem decided?
rows.a: The status die is rolled and picks one of the six status effects at random. Tri Attack and Power Gem only roll it when a status symbol appears in the attack roll.

rows.q: When Memento or Perish Song raises battle fatigue to 5, is fatigue damage taken immediately?
rows.a: No. Battle fatigue damage is taken when dice are rolled, so it starts with the next roll.

rows.q: Does Calm Mind's "current battle fatigue" include the fatigue gained from this roll?
rows.a: Yes. The battle fatigue gained from this roll is counted too.

rows.q: For moves that also inflict a status effect on another Pokémon in the opposing party (Shocking Verity, Blazing Valor, Chilling Acuity), what happens if the active opponent is immune or already has a status effect?
rows.a: The other Pokémon is still affected, because the move inflicts the status on the two Pokémon separately.

rows.q: With those moves, who chooses if the opposing party has several "other Pokémon"?
rows.a: The attacking side chooses from the non-fainted Pokémon. If there is no other Pokémon, as with a wild Pokémon, that part does not happen.

rows.q: Do type effectiveness or double damage apply to the 2 damage Earthquake and Prismatic Laser deal to other Pokémon?
rows.a: No. It is fixed damage dealt by an effect.

rows.q: If a Pokémon on my Bench faints from that damage, does the wild Pokémon flee?
rows.a: No. A wild Pokémon only flees when your active Pokémon faints. Your active Pokémon and the turn order also stay as they are.

rows.q: Does Heal Bell also heal fainted Pokémon in the party?
rows.a: No. A fainted Pokémon can only be brought back by a full heal.

rows.q: When a wild Pokémon or a Team Galactic Pokémon uses Belch, does it consume an Apricorn to increase its attack strength?
rows.a: No. Wild Pokémon and Team Galactic have no Apricorns, so they cannot increase Belch's attack strength. They cannot use the opponent's Apricorns instead either.

rows.q: Who chooses the colour of the Apricorn lost to Bug Bite? What if it is used on a wild Pokémon or a Team Galactic Pokémon?
rows.a: The trainer of the attacked Pokémon chooses one from their own bag. Wild Pokémon and Team Galactic have no Apricorns, so nothing happens.

rows.q: Do moves that let you choose a type (Hidden Power, Hidden Punch, Multi-Attack, Judgement) also change the Pokémon's type?
rows.a: No. Only the type of that attack changes; the Pokémon's type stays the same.

rows.q: When switching out with U-Turn, Volt Switch, Flip Turn, Teleport or Shelter, is Poisoned damage taken before the switch?
rows.a: Yes. The switch from these moves happens after the turn ends, so end-of-turn effects such as Poisoned come first.

rows.q: Are there times when even a switching move cannot switch the user out?
rows.a: If the user is Frozen, is under an effect that prevents switching out or fleeing, or has had its switch blocked this turn by Blast Crystal, it cannot switch out even with a switching move.

rows.q: Can moves used from your party (Lunge, Acrobatics) be used while your active Pokémon is Frozen?
rows.a: Yes. They can be used even if your active Pokémon is Frozen or prevented from switching out.

rows.q: Can a Pokémon still come in with Lunge or Acrobatics while Fairy Lock is in effect?
rows.a: No. Fairy Lock prevents switching out using move effects, so it blocks these moves too.

rows.q: Which damage taken by the user do Outrage, Raging Fury, Petal Dance and Thrash also deal to the target?
rows.a: The damage the user took during that attack (from Confused, battle fatigue and so on), in the exact amount taken. Galactic Retribution, which is taken at the end of the turn, is not included.

rows.q: What if the user is immune to the Confused status those moves inflict on it? Does it take Confused damage on this same attack?
rows.a: If it is immune, it does not become Confused. A Confused status inflicted by this attack deals no damage on this attack.

rows.q: When Barrier turns critical hits back, how much does the attacker take?
rows.a: The attacker takes the critical hit share of that roll (the critical hit faces plus any extra damage attached to critical hits) instead. Type effectiveness, double damage and the Burned reduction do not apply to the returned damage, and the rest of the damage is taken by the Barrier user as usual.

rows.q: Does the "first attack" of Blast Crystal or Star Shield apply again after switching out and coming back in?
rows.a: No. Only once per battle.

rows.q: What if two Pokémon in the party each hold a Star Shield?
rows.a: It applies once in that battle for each Pokémon holding one.

rows.q: Which move is a Pokémon holding a Choice Band locked into?
rows.a: The first move it chooses after coming in, and the lock lasts until it leaves play.

rows.q: How are Eviolite's "Weak/Moderate Pokémon" and "Pokémon that are not fully evolved" judged?
rows.a: The tier is the encounter tier on the card, and Starter Pokémon are included. A Pokémon that still has a card to evolve into counts as not fully evolved.

rows.q: Can Alluring Stew only be used on capture rolls?
rows.a: No. It can be used on either an attack roll or a capture roll.

rows.q: How long does Alluring Stew's effect last? Can I decide when to use it?
rows.a: It can be used once in the next wild battle on the turn it was made, and it is lost when that turn ends even if unused. When a status symbol appears in a roll, you decide for yourself whether to use it.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: Does the health that sets the attack strength of Eruption, Heavy Slam and Seismic Toss include the extra health of an Alpha Pokémon?
rows.a: Yes. Heavy Slam and Seismic Toss count maximum health including the extra health from Alpha Pokémon, and Eruption counts the health currently remaining.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: Which initiative sets Electro Ball's attack strength?
rows.a: Half the user's current initiative, rounded down, after all modifiers such as Paralysed (−3) or Swiftness Sash (+2), up to a maximum of 5.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: How is the attack strength of Flail and Revenge counted?
rows.a: Flail gets 1 for every 2 damage on the user at the moment the move is used. Revenge counts the fainted Pokémon on the user's own side, and this is the same when a Team Galactic Pokémon uses it.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: For "+1 attack strength for each Pokémon with a Song move", what is a Song move, and is the user itself counted?
rows.a: A move whose name ends in "Song" (including Perish Song). The user is not counted; only the other non-fainted Pokémon in the party are. Surf works the same way.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: What is the "damage taken last turn" for Destiny Bond and Rampart Riposte?
rows.a: All the damage that Pokémon took on the turn just before (usually the opponent's turn); attack strength is increased by that amount.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: Does the attack strength of Rollout and Lift Off reset when the user switches out?
rows.a: No. It increases by the number of times that Pokémon has used the move in that battle, and the count stays after switching out. Uses by other Pokémon are not counted.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: Is the attack strength Foul Play copies the value after modifiers?
rows.a: No. It is the attack strength printed on the opponent's move card. If the move's attack strength is "?", it is the value worked out for the Pokémon that knows the move, or 1 if that cannot be determined.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: When Mimic uses the target's move, do its type and effect come with it? While Confused, which move counts as the one used?
rows.a: Attack strength, type and effect all follow the selected move. The move used is still Mimic, though, so the Confused "same move" check looks at Mimic.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: If an effect copied with Kinesis has a use limit, whose uses are spent?
rows.a: The uses of the Pokémon that used Kinesis. Effects that set attack strength are copied too, and effects that do not stack still do not stack when copied.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: Can Sacred Sword's dice be rerolled with Change of Fate (Dialga)?
rows.a: No. Sacred Sword's dice cannot be replaced, removed or rerolled by any effect. Type effectiveness applies as usual.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: Do effects that add dice faces (Bulk Up and so on) apply to Sacred Sword?
rows.a: Yes. Only replacing and removing are blocked, so adding still applies.

rows.sectionTitle: Battle — Variable Attack Strength · Copying Moves
rows.q: Is the healing from Giga Drain and Power Whip reduced by how much health the target has left?
rows.a: No. The user heals for half the final calculated damage, rounded down, regardless of the target's remaining health.

rows.q: Can I throw a ball with a move that says "the user may use a second move this turn" (Quick Attack, Mach Punch, Shadow Sneak, Extreme Speed, Bullet Punch, Aqua Jet)?
rows.a: No. The second action can only be a move.

rows.q: If the second move is another one of those moves, can I use a third move as well?
rows.a: No. This effect does not chain.

rows.q: Can the second move be the same move again?
rows.a: Yes.

rows.q: If the first attack makes the target faint, can the second move be used on the next Pokémon?
rows.a: No. In that case there is no second move, and the effect counts as unused, so the use is kept.

rows.q: If I choose not to use the second move, is the "once until the user switches out" use kept?
rows.a: No. The use counts as spent even if you do not use it.

rows.q: If two moves were used in one turn, which one is "the move used last turn" on the next turn?
rows.a: The one used second.

rows.q: On a turn with a second move, how many times do end-of-turn effects such as Poisoned happen?
rows.a: Only once, after both attacks are finished.

rows.q: If the final move from Encore heals the user, does it avoid fainting?
rows.a: No. Whatever the final move does, the user faints afterwards.

rows.q: If the attacker also fainted during that attack from battle fatigue or recoil, can the Encore final move still be used?
rows.a: No. If the attacker has already fainted, there is no final move.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: Who chooses the move for a wild Legendary Pokémon or an Alpha Pokémon?
rows.a: In the original game, another player chooses, or you follow the Ultra Beast principle (signature move first, otherwise the move with the highest value).

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: In this game, who chooses moves for Pokémon no player controls?
rows.a: The game chooses for them. In the Heart of Sinnoh campaign, Team Galactic can be controlled by another player depending on the room settings, but opponents in the Ultra Burst campaign are always controlled by the game.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: Are there several copies of each Legendary Pokémon card? Can I meet a Legendary Pokémon again after it has been captured or defeated?
rows.a: There is only one copy of each Legendary Pokémon card. Once someone captures or defeats it, it won't appear again in that game.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: If I lose to a Legendary Pokémon at a Legendary Location, can I challenge it again?
rows.a: Yes. If you lose or forfeit, the Legendary Pokémon card returns to the deck, so you can challenge it again.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: If I enter a tile with a Legendary Pokémon that appeared at a Shrine, do I have to battle it?
rows.a: No. Only Alpha Pokémon and other trainers force a battle.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: How is the type of Alpha Strike decided? Do type effectiveness and bonuses follow that type too?
rows.a: Choose one of the types that Pokémon can learn. Type effectiveness and the Power bonuses from the Heart of Sinnoh and Artifacts all use the chosen type.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: Does Alpha Strike's "Power 2 if used on the previous turn" carry over when I switch Pokémon? What if I choose a different type?
rows.a: It is tracked separately for each Pokémon. It is the same move even with a different type chosen, so if the same Pokémon uses it twice in a row, its Power drops to 2.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: Do Alpha Pokémon use both their signature move and Alpha Strike?
rows.a: Yes, they can use both.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: Does the "+1 Power on the next attack" from Beast Boost remain if the Pokémon switches out?
rows.a: No. It is lost when that Pokémon switches out.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: What happens to damage taken when a Pokémon changes form during a battle?
rows.a: It stays as it is. Battle fatigue and the turn order don't change either.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: With a move that picks a type and changes form (Adaptive Cloak), does the chosen type apply even if I don't change form?
rows.a: Yes. You can choose a type without changing form, and the chosen type applies starting with the attack that used the move.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: Can a Celestial Artifact change the form of a God of Sinnoh?
rows.a: Yes. Like Shaymin with the Gracidea Flower or Rotom with the Secret Key, a God holding its Celestial Artifact can change form outside of battle.

rows.sectionTitle: Legendary Pokémon · Legendary special moves · Forms
rows.q: What happens if the Artifact that changed a Pokémon's form is removed or taken away?
rows.a: The Pokémon returns to its base form.

rows.q: How many times can I play Change of Fate in one turn?
rows.a: You can play 1 effect on your turn outside of battle and 1 effect per battle turn inside a battle, and the two are counted separately. Even on a turn where you played Palkia while moving, you can still play Dialga in the battle that follows.

rows.q: Can I play Change of Fate in another trainer's battle?
rows.a: No. You can only play it in your own battles. If you are one of the battlers, you can play it even when the battle happens on another trainer's turn.

rows.q: Can I use a Play 3 effect with only my Follower token and Arceus cards?
rows.a: No. You need at least 1 actual card of that God.

rows.q: If I hold matching cards together with Arceus cards, which ones are spent first for a Play 3?
rows.a: You choose how many Arceus cards to include.

rows.q: What happens when I have 6 Change of Fate cards?
rows.a: You immediately choose cards to discard until you have 5. You may discard the card you just received, and you choose right away even on another trainer's turn.

rows.q: Can a Dialga card also make my opponent reroll their dice?
rows.a: Yes. If it is your battle, you can play it on your opponent's attack roll too. The same goes for the Play 3 effect.

rows.q: Can a Dialga card reroll dice that were added by a move's effect?
rows.a: Yes, they can be rerolled.

rows.q: Do Drowsy, Paralysed or held-item dice changes apply again to dice rerolled with a Dialga card?
rows.a: No. Effects that change dice apply only once per attack.

rows.q: Can a Dialga card reroll dice that were removed by Paralysed and similar effects?
rows.a: Yes, you can pick them.

rows.q: Does rerolling with a Dialga card increase battle fatigue?
rows.a: No, it doesn't.

rows.q: With Dialga's Play 3 effect, can I reroll dice one at a time and decide on the next die after seeing each result?
rows.a: No. You choose all the dice to reroll at once and roll them together.

rows.q: Can I play a Dialga card on a capture roll?
rows.a: Yes. You can play it after rolling the Ball and before the result is decided.

rows.q: Can I play a Palkia card after using up my movement? Can I keep walking after teleporting?
rows.a: Yes to both. A Palkia card uses no movement, and you can act as usual on the tile you arrive at.

rows.q: Can I escape from a battle with a Palkia card?
rows.a: No. A Palkia card can only be played on your turn outside of battle.

rows.q: Can Palkia's Play 3 effect take me to the Distortion World?
rows.a: Only in the Ultra Burst campaign. In the Heart of Sinnoh campaign, Distortion World tiles can't be chosen.

rows.q: How much HP does Giratina's Play 3 effect spend, and how much Power does it add?
rows.a: It spends all remaining HP and adds half that amount (rounded down) to Power. With 7 HP left, that is +3 Power.

rows.q: If a Pokémon reduced to 0 HP by a Giratina effect uses a healing move, does it avoid fainting?
rows.a: No, it faints. The move is carried out in full, but the Pokémon doesn't receive the healing.

rows.q: Can I play a Giratina card on an opposing Pokémon?
rows.a: No. You can only play it on your own Pokémon, before it attacks.

rows.q: Do the status effects and held items of a Pokémon reduced to 0 HP by a Giratina effect still apply to that attack?
rows.a: No. That Pokémon's own status effects, held items and ongoing effects are not applied; only the effects of the move itself are resolved.

rows.q: Does an Arceus card do anything when played alone? What about Arceus's Play 3 effect?
rows.a: It has no single-card effect; it counts as any 1 card toward another card's Play 3 effect. Arceus's Play 3 effect (1 Blessing of Arceus) can only be used in the Ultra Burst campaign.

rows.q: What can I take from my opponent when I win a trainer battle?
rows.a: You choose 1 Artifact or take up to 2 Change of Fate cards at random. You can take an Artifact that one of their Pokémon is holding, but you can't take Battle Items, the Scroll of Nobility or the Heart of Sinnoh.

rows.q: Can I trade with or challenge another trainer just by passing through their tile while moving?
rows.a: No. You have to stop on the same tile as that trainer. The only thing you can do while passing is reveal a Hidden Spot.

rows.q: Can I keep moving after trading with another trainer?
rows.a: Yes. After stopping on the tile to trade, you can keep moving with your remaining movement. A challenge is a battle, so your turn ends when it is over.

rows.q: My challenge was declined. Can I challenge the same trainer again on the same turn?
rows.a: No. You can't challenge a trainer who declined again on that turn.

rows.q: What can be exchanged in a trade?
rows.a: You can exchange Apricorns, Journey Points, Balls, items in your Bag, Pokémon in your party and Change of Fate cards. Shards, the Heart of Sinnoh, Journey Stamps, Follower tokens and Trainer Cards can't be traded.

rows.q: Can I give something without receiving anything in return?
rows.a: Yes.

rows.q: When a Pokémon is traded, what happens to its learned moves and held items?
rows.a: Its learned moves, held items, Alpha token, damage and status effects all go with the Pokémon.

rows.q: Are there Pokémon that can't be traded?
rows.a: A Pokémon with a breach card attached or one holding the Heart of Sinnoh can't be traded (you can remove the Heart first). Also, both trainers must have at least 1 Pokémon left after the trade.

rows.q: Does trading use movement or end my turn? How many times can I trade per turn?
rows.a: It uses no movement, doesn't end your turn, and has no limit on the number of trades.

rows.q: Can remote trades with a trainer who follows the same God only be made on my turn?
rows.a: No. You can also propose one on another trainer's turn. However, neither of you may be in a battle.

rows.q: Is a remote challenge impossible to decline if the target is outside a village?
rows.a: No. A remote challenge can always be declined, wherever the target is.

rows.q: When can I make a remote challenge? Do I need movement left?
rows.a: Only on your turn, and movement doesn't matter. You can't challenge a trainer who is protected from challenges or whom you have already challenged that turn, and your turn ends when the battle is over.

rows.q: Does a Pokémon received in a trade count as "gained" for Trainer Card unlock conditions?
rows.a: No. Only Pokémon you captured or gained through a card effect count.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: How many times do I have to battle the Grunt in Act I?
rows.a: One battle. The Grunt's 2 Pokémon come as one party, and you must defeat both in a single battle with a Pokémon of your own still standing.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Do I gain Journey Points for beating Team Galactic?
rows.a: No. You don't gain Journey Points for defeating Team Galactic Pokémon.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: When battling a Commander, which is decided first: the Commander's Pokémon or my lead Pokémon?
rows.a: The Commander's side chooses and reveals its Pokémon first, and then the challenger sends out their first Pokémon.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Can the player controlling Team Galactic play Change of Fate in that battle?
rows.a: No. Change of Fate can only be played in your own battles, so the player controlling Team Galactic can't play it.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: When is the damage stored in Galactic Retribution transferred?
rows.a: After a Team Galactic Pokémon is attacked, it is transferred at the end of the attacker's turn. The attack lands as normal, and the transferred damage is applied together with end-of-turn damage such as Poisoned.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Does Galactic Retribution come back on the attack that defeats the last Team Galactic Pokémon?
rows.a: No. If that attack ends the battle, Galactic Retribution doesn't trigger.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Do the 2 damage stored for the Team Galactic Pokémon I just defeated come back on that same attack?
rows.a: No. Those 2 are only stored, and can be transferred the next time a Team Galactic Pokémon is attacked.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Do type effectiveness, Burned or Prism Armour apply to damage transferred by Galactic Retribution?
rows.a: No. It is fixed damage rather than an attack, so type effectiveness, doubling, damage reduction and damage caps don't apply.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Does Galactic Retribution trigger on an attack that misses or deals 0 damage?
rows.a: Yes. If you attacked with a move, the Pokémon counts as having been attacked. Damage such as Poisoned or battle fatigue is not an attack, so it doesn't trigger.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Does the damage stored in Galactic Retribution carry over to the next battle?
rows.a: No. It lasts only within that battle and is 0 when a battle starts.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: If I attack with a move that switches out after attacking, who takes Galactic Retribution?
rows.a: The Pokémon that attacked. Galactic Retribution is resolved first, and the switch happens afterwards.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: When can a Team Galactic Pokémon use Plan B?
rows.a: Any Team Galactic Pokémon can always choose it in place of its own moves.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: In Act I, if my last Pokémon and the Grunt's last Pokémon faint together, have I completed the objective?
rows.a: No. It is a draw, so the objective is not completed.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: If I challenge the Grunt again after losing, do the same Pokémon appear?
rows.a: No. Each time you challenge, the Grunt deck is reshuffled and 2 new Pokémon are drawn.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: What happens if a battle against a Commander or Cyrus ends in a draw?
rows.a: It counts as a loss. To win, you must have a Pokémon left that can still battle.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: If I challenge a Commander or Cyrus again after losing, does the damage I dealt in the earlier battle remain?
rows.a: No. When the battle ends, the cards return to the deck, and when you challenge again the opponent's Pokémon are chosen anew.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: In Act III, which Apricorn do I have to offer to restore the Heart of Sinnoh? Do the Shards disappear?
rows.a: After collecting the three Shards, offer 1 Apricorn of any colour at the Origin Shrine. The Shards stay with you, and your turn continues.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Does one of my Pokémon have to hold the Heart of Sinnoh to challenge Cyrus?
rows.a: No. Once you have restored the Heart, you can challenge him even if no Pokémon is holding it.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Does the Heart of Sinnoh also raise the Power of Typeless moves or Plan B?
rows.a: No. Only moves of the same type as the holder gain +1 Power.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: When someone chooses to be the Traitor, is the battle that follows the same as a normal trainer battle?
rows.a: No. The Traitor becomes the challenger and holds Initiative Advantage, and the opponent can't decline. There is no challenge protection and no victory reward either.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Who wins if the battle against the Traitor ends in a draw?
rows.a: The Traitor counts as having lost, so the opposing trainer wins.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: What happens if I choose to be the Traitor in a solo game?
rows.a: There is no other trainer to defeat, so the game ends immediately with the Traitor's victory.

rows.sectionTitle: Team Galactic · Heart of Sinnoh campaign
rows.q: Can I meet the Lake Guardians (Azelf, Uxie and Mesprit) in the Heart of Sinnoh campaign?
rows.a: No. Only the Ultra Burst campaign lets you battle the Lake Guardians separately.

rows.q: Is the "once per turn" limit on Shrine offerings counted separately for each Shrine?
rows.a: No. It is once per turn across all Shrines. On your next turn you can make an offering at the same Shrine again.

rows.q: When I pay 7 Journey Points to draw 3 cards, do I still have to offer an Apricorn? How are the 2 chosen cards resolved?
rows.a: You still have to offer an Apricorn. Choose and resolve one card, and after seeing the result, choose the next one from the remaining cards.

rows.q: Does the offering made in Act III to restore the Heart of Sinnoh also draw a Shrine event card?
rows.a: Yes. The offering that restores the Heart is a Shrine offering, so you draw a card and it counts as your one offering for that turn.

rows.q: When a Shrine blessing is shared with another trainer and there is a choice to make, who makes it?
rows.a: Each trainer who receives the blessing chooses for their own share.

rows.q: With 4 or more trainers, are Legendary events and Celestial Fractures also shared with another trainer?
rows.a: No. Only Shrine blessings are shared with one other trainer of your choice. Legendary events and Celestial Fractures affect all trainers, as written on the card.

rows.q: Are the colours of the Apricorns from Unexpected Gift fixed?
rows.a: No. You can choose any colours, including several of the same colour.

rows.q: What does a Pokémon swapped through Equivalent Exchange keep?
rows.a: Its learned moves, held items, Alpha token, damage and status effects all remain. Its signature move changes to that of the new card.

rows.q: In Equivalent Exchange, which tier do Starter Pokémon and Alpha Pokémon count as?
rows.a: Starter Pokémon count as Weak Pokémon, and Alpha Pokémon count as Strong Pokémon, following their card's tier. The replacement card can only be chosen from the same tier.

rows.q: Can Ancient Wisdom teach a move from a lower-tier Pokémon? What about Pokémon with several forms?
rows.a: Yes. You can choose a lower tier, and for a card with several forms you can also choose the signature move of another form.

rows.q: After drawing Ancient Wisdom, can I release a Pokémon and then learn that Pokémon's move?
rows.a: No. You can only choose moves of Pokémon that were in the discard pile when the card was drawn.

rows.q: Can Ancient Wisdom teach a move of a type the Pokémon can't learn?
rows.a: No. As usual, you can only teach moves of a type it can learn.

rows.q: Does a stew gained from Splendid Banquet count toward the "each kind of stew once per turn" limit?
rows.a: No. The banquet's stew is counted separately, so you can craft the same stew yourself on the same turn and stack the effects (two Zesty Stews give +6 movement).

rows.q: What happens if a Legendary event card is drawn but that Legendary Pokémon has already left the game?
rows.a: No token is placed, and everyone still receives the Apricorns shown on the card.

rows.q: What happens to the token if I lose to a Legendary Pokémon placed at a Shrine?
rows.a: The token stays at that Shrine, and no offerings can be made there while it remains.

rows.q: When a Celestial Fracture comes up, do I have to choose a God?
rows.a: If you are not a Follower yet, you don't have to choose.

rows.q: Once I have become a Follower, can I go back to following no God?
rows.a: No. You can switch to another God, but you can't go back.

rows.q: Can I change my Follower token every time I draw a Change of Fate card?
rows.a: No. You can only change it when a Celestial Fracture comes up.

rows.q: Can I follow a God that has already been captured or defeated and has left the game?
rows.a: No. A God that has left the game can't be chosen and isn't included when Followers are counted.

rows.q: Who decides when two or more Gods are tied for the most Followers?
rows.a: The trainer who drew the Celestial Fracture card chooses.

rows.q: Which God descends if nobody follows any God?
rows.a: No God descends. The Origin Shrine stays as it is.

rows.q: If a God of Sinnoh is already at the Origin Shrine and another God descends, does the first God leave the game?
rows.a: No. Only its token is removed, so it can descend again at a later Celestial Fracture.

rows.q: If the Act III offering to restore the Heart draws a Celestial Fracture and a God descends, what happens to the Heart?
rows.a: The Heart is already restored. You can go on to Cyrus without battling the God that descended.

rows.q: If the God I follow descends in the middle of my turn, does my movement go up by 1 right away?
rows.a: No. The Follower's +1 movement is checked at the start of a turn, so it applies from your next turn.

rows.q: If the Change of Fate card from a Celestial Fracture puts me over the hand limit, what do I do first?
rows.a: Discard the excess cards first, then choose your Follower.

rows.q: If I enter the Origin Shrine while a God of Sinnoh is there, do I have to battle it?
rows.a: No. The battle starts only when you Search on that tile. The same goes for Legendary Pokémon placed at Shrines.

rows.q: To negate the Celestial Aura, does a Pokémon have to hold the Celestial Artifact?
rows.a: No. You only need to have it in your Bag.

rows.q: Can a God with the Celestial Aura only be captured in its second form?
rows.a: No. It can be captured in its first form too, on a roll of 7 or higher. With the matching Artifact it is 6, as for other Legendary Pokémon.

rows.q: When a God's first form is defeated and its second form appears, how is the turn order decided?
rows.a: Initiative is compared again to set the order, just as when a new Pokémon comes in.

rows.q: What happens to the God token if I lose to or forfeit against a God of Sinnoh?
rows.a: It stays at the Origin Shrine.

rows.q: Do I get an extra turn if I capture a God of Sinnoh instead of defeating it?
rows.a: Yes. A capture counts as a win. The extra turn is only granted in the Heart of Sinnoh campaign.

rows.q: If I never met the second form because I had the Celestial Artifact, can I still learn the signature move of the defeated God's other form?
rows.a: Yes. When you defeat a Pokémon whose forms have different signature moves, you can teach any one of them.

rows.q: Do the Pokémon in a Swarm Battle also follow the tile's climate?
rows.a: No. Only the biome set for each Gate is used.

rows.q: Who holds Initiative Advantage in a Swarm Battle?
rows.a: You do, as the one who started the battle. The wild side holds Initiative Advantage only for Alpha Pokémon.

rows.q: Does the battle end if I capture a Pokémon during a Swarm Battle?
rows.a: No. The next Pokémon comes in just as if you had defeated it, and you can switch your own Pokémon in between.

rows.q: Can I teach the moves of Pokémon I defeated in a Swarm Battle? What if I lose the battle?
rows.a: Yes, you can. Even if you lose the battle, you can teach the moves of the Pokémon you defeated, but you don't gain Journey Points.

rows.q: Are stamp rewards determined by the position of the stamp slot?
rows.a: No. They are determined by how many stamps you have collected so far. You can't choose a lower-level reward instead.

rows.q: Can I earn a stamp on another trainer's turn?
rows.a: Yes. In this game, you automatically receive the stamp and its reward as soon as you meet the condition, on anyone's turn.

rows.q: How do I earn the "Fail to capture 2 turns in a row" stamp?
rows.a: You must actually throw a Ball and fail twice in a row in a single battle. Using a move in between resets the count.

rows.q: Do I earn the "Beat a trainer" stamp for beating Team Galactic? Can I get it through a trade?
rows.a: Beating Team Galactic earns it only in a solo game. It can't be earned through a trade.

rows.q: Do I earn the "Capture a Legendary" stamp if I gain a Legendary Pokémon through a trade or another effect?
rows.a: No. You earn it only when you capture one yourself by throwing a Ball. Capturing an Alpha Pokémon also earns it.

rows.q: Do Artifacts or Alpha tokens count toward the "3 held items" stamp?
rows.a: Artifacts held by your Pokémon count. Alpha tokens are not held items, so they don't count.

rows.q: For the "3 different Change of Fate cards" stamp, can an Arceus card count as any card?
rows.a: No. Arceus cards count as just one kind. You need three different kinds out of the four in your hand.

rows.q: What happens to the 5 Pokémon cards drawn as a stamp reward?
rows.a: They are drawn at random from the deck and can't be chosen. These cards leave the encounter deck and can no longer be encountered, and you keep their signature moves like move cards to teach later.

rows.q: What if the deck has fewer than 5 cards when I receive the reward?
rows.a: You draw as many as are left.

rows.q: With the Scroll of Nobility, can every Starter Pokémon in my party use its Noble Form?
rows.a: No. Only a fully evolved Starter Pokémon holding the Scroll can use it. You decide whether to change form, and removing the Scroll returns it to its original form.

rows.q: Does a Noble Form count as a Legendary Pokémon? Can the Scroll of Nobility be taken as a trainer battle reward?
rows.a: A Noble Form counts as a Legendary Pokémon. The Scroll is not an Artifact, so it can't be taken.

rows.q: Do I have to use the Trainer Card Expansion? Which campaigns is it for?
rows.a: It is an optional expansion, and it can be used in both the Heart of Sinnoh and Ultra Burst campaigns.

rows.q: Does "defeat" in the unlock conditions only mean wild Pokémon?
rows.a: No. Pokémon in a Swarm Battle and other trainers' Pokémon also count, as long as they are Moderate or Strong Pokémon.

rows.q: Does defeating a Team Galactic Pokémon or an Ultra Beast unlock an ability?
rows.a: No. Only Pokémon whose card shows the Moderate or Strong tier icon count. Team Galactic Pokémon, starter Pokémon, Ultra Beasts and Necrozma do not.

rows.q: Does it count if one of my Pokémon evolves into a Moderate or Strong Pokémon?
rows.a: Yes. Evolving counts as obtaining it.

rows.q: Does capturing or defeating a Legendary Pokémon or an Alpha Pokémon unlock the Red ability?
rows.a: No. Legendary Pokémon and Alpha Pokémon do not count as Strong Pokémon.

rows.q: If I capture a Strong Pokémon before my Blue ability is unlocked, does the Red ability unlock too?
rows.a: No. The abilities unlock in order: Blue with a Moderate Pokémon first, then Red with a Strong Pokémon.

rows.q: Does a Strong Pokémon I captured before unlocking Blue count towards Red once Blue is unlocked?
rows.a: No. You must defeat or obtain another Strong Pokémon after Blue is unlocked.

rows.q: Have I "defeated" the opposing Pokémon if it faints from poison or battle fatigue rather than my attack?
rows.a: Yes. If the opposing Pokémon faints in a battle you fought, it counts as defeated no matter what made it faint.

rows.q: My party is full and I release the Pokémon I just captured straight away. Did I still "obtain" it?
rows.a: Yes. It counts as obtained the moment the capture succeeds.

rows.q: Can an ability with no stated limit be used any number of times?
rows.a: Yes. Unless the card states a limit such as "once per turn", it applies every time its condition is met.

rows.q: Can I always choose whether to use a trainer card ability?
rows.a: Only abilities worded with "you may" are optional; the rest always apply. For example, the Ninja Boy's Toxin Dart must inflict Poisoned, Confused or Drowsy whenever you use Initiative Advantage. You still choose whether to use Initiative Advantage at all.

rows.q: Do abilities that affect rolls apply to capture rolls too?
rows.a: Abilities worded with "attack" apply to attack rolls only. Abilities that say "all rolls", or that do not name a kind of roll, also apply to capture rolls. The Guitarist's Ramp Up increases the Amplifier for status symbols rolled in a capture roll as well.

rows.q: Does the Ace Trainer's "Strong Pokémon gain +1 initiative" apply to Alpha Pokémon?
rows.a: No. It does not apply to a Pokémon with the Alpha Pokémon token attached.

rows.q: How are the Artist's "moves of every type" counted?
rows.a: Count both the signature moves and the learned moves of the Pokémon in your party. A Typeless move, Alpha Strike or Beast Boost each stands in for any one type.

rows.q: Does the Beauty's "critical hits deal +2 damage, status symbols deal -1 damage" apply to capture rolls?
rows.a: Yes. It applies to all your rolls, so it is included in the total of a capture roll.

rows.q: With both Beauty abilities unlocked, what happens to status symbols when I attack with a Normal-type or Dark-type move?
rows.a: The -1 and +1 cancel out, so status symbols deal no bonus or penalty damage and only the +2 for critical hits remains.

rows.q: Does a Pokémon with both types get the Hiker's bonus twice?
rows.a: No. A Rock/Ground dual-type Pokémon still gets it only once.

rows.q: Do the Gardener (Grass, Rock) and the Delinquent (Dark, Poison) also apply only once to dual-type Pokémon?
rows.a: Yes. As with the Hiker, the bonus applies once.

rows.q: What counts as "damage taken from attacks" for the Delinquent, Bird Keeper, Poké Fan and Roller Skater?
rows.a: Attack damage, and damage a move effect deals to other Pokémon, such as Earthquake. Recoil, battle fatigue, status effects, Galactic Retribution and damage reflected by Barrier do not count.

rows.q: Does the Ruin Maniac's "+1 attack strength from Artifact bonuses" apply to every Artifact?
rows.a: No. It only applies to Artifacts that already give an attack strength bonus. Artifacts without one, such as a Celestial Artifact, gain nothing.

rows.q: Does the Scientist's +1 apply when type effectiveness is neutral?
rows.a: No. The +1 only applies when there is bonus damage from type effectiveness.

rows.q: Do the Team Aqua and Team Magma abilities only apply to my own Pokémon?
rows.a: No. In any battle you take part in, they apply equally to the opposing Pokémon and its moves.

rows.q: Do starter Pokémon count as "Weak Pokémon" for trainer cards?
rows.a: Yes. Starter Pokémon are treated as Weak Pokémon. A Pokémon with the Alpha Pokémon token attached is not.

rows.q: Does the Fairy Tale Girl's "+1 healing" apply to effects that fully restore a Pokémon?
rows.a: No. Full restores are unchanged; every other healing effect heals 1 more. It does not apply when Poisoned prevented the healing.

rows.q: If an ability that raised maximum health is lost (the Pokémon is traded away or changes form) and its damage now equals or exceeds its maximum health, does it faint?
rows.a: No. In this game it does not faint and is left with 1 health.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: Can the Hex Maniac's Unstable Magic be used when an opponent inflicts a status effect on my Pokémon?
rows.a: No. It can only be used when your own Pokémon inflicts a status effect.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: Can I roll the status dice with Unstable Magic if the opponent is immune to the status I would have inflicted?
rows.a: Yes. The status you roll is then applied under the usual rules.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: How many status effects can the Hex Maniac's Spell Caster stack?
rows.a: There is no limit. You can add one of each status effect the opponent does not already have.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: Can I use the Chef's Masterwork Stew several times in one battle to raise attack strength further?
rows.a: No. It can be used once per battle.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: When is Masterwork Stew used?
rows.a: Before you roll the dice for your attack. From then on its effect lasts until the battle ends, including for Pokémon you switch in.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: For Essentia's Opportune Strike, what counts as a "wild Pokémon" and as "not having moved"?
rows.a: Wild Pokémon include Swarms, Alpha Pokémon, Legendary Pokémon and Gods, but not trainers, Team Galactic or Ultra Beasts. Travelling by Fly, Teleport or a Distortion Gate counts as moving, just like walking.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: Can the Ninja Boy use Initiative Advantage when his Pokémon is already faster?
rows.a: Only once Toxin Dart is unlocked. Using it passes the token to the opponent as usual and inflicts the status effect.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: Can the Poké Maniac's Pokémon Disguise use the opponent's learned moves?
rows.a: No. It can only use the signature move of the opposing Pokémon currently in battle.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: When is the Psychic's Subtle Manipulation used?
rows.a: After the dice are rolled, at the same time a Dialga card would reroll them. You can still respond after an opponent forces a reroll, and you can use it once per attack.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: Does a Typeless move count as one of the three types for the Triathlete's Triple Threat?
rows.a: Yes. Typeless counts as a type, and you can also change an attack to Typeless.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: Rolls · Attack Strength · Types
rows.q: Can I decide whether to use the Veteran's Gale Force after seeing the roll?
rows.a: Yes. Right after rolling, you choose to add 1 status symbol, 2 status symbols or none.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Does the Aroma Lady's Natural Remedy stack with the healing of a draining move such as Giga Drain?
rows.a: Yes. It is added separately on top of the move's own healing.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Does Natural Remedy count damage dealt beyond the opponent's remaining health?
rows.a: Yes. The user heals half the damage the attack dealt, rounded up, regardless of the opponent's remaining health.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Does the Undivided Acolyte's Judgement of Arceus trigger after an attack that dealt no damage?
rows.a: Yes. After you attack, the opposing Pokémon in battle always faints if it has 2 or less health remaining.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Does the Worker's Road Works trigger for a Steel-type Pokémon sent out at the start of a battle?
rows.a: No. It only triggers when the Pokémon is switched in during the battle or sent in as your next Pokémon. The block on switching out and fleeing lasts until that Steel-type Pokémon leaves the battle.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Can Team Rocket's Pokémon Thief capture Team Galactic's Pokémon?
rows.a: No. It can only be used in trainer battles against other players.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Can Pokémon Thief capture the opponent's last Pokémon?
rows.a: No.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: What happens to the trainer whose Pokémon was stolen?
rows.a: They send in their next Pokémon as if that Pokémon had fainted, and they may also forfeit. If they have no usable Pokémon left, they lose.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Can I stay on my current tile with Team Rocket's Blasting Off?
rows.a: Yes.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Can Blasting Off really take me to any tile?
rows.a: Not to tiles in the Distortion World. You are fully restored at the start of your next turn, as the card says.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Does the Expert's Legendary Protector add to the normal effect of Beast Boost?
rows.a: No, it replaces it. Your Legendary Pokémon only heal 3 damage, reset their battle fatigue to 0 and gain +2 attack strength on their next attack.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Can Hyper Potion be used on the Pokémon currently in battle?
rows.a: Yes. The Pokémon in battle is still a Pokémon in your party.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: When the Kindler's Burning Ignition inflicts Burned, does a "double damage if the target is Burned" effect apply to that same attack?
rows.a: Not to that attack. It applies from the next attack onwards.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: With the Black Belt's Fighting Spirit and the Fairy Tale Girl's Day Dreamer, can I choose which Pokémon receive the status? Can I inflict it on an immune Pokémon?
rows.a: You choose for each Pokémon. A Pokémon immune to that status (for example, a Fire type to Burned) cannot receive it.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Battle: After Damage · Fainting · Switching
rows.q: Can Fighting Spirit inflict Burned on Pokémon that are not Fighting types?
rows.a: Yes. They get the normal Burned effect.

rows.q: Can the 2 free tiles of the Hiker, Picnicker, Roller Skater, Swimmer and Triathlete be split up?
rows.a: No. They must be used one after the other. If you move 1 free tile and then take a normal step, the other free tile is lost.

rows.q: Can I interact with the tile I pass through between the two free tiles?
rows.a: Yes.

rows.q: Do lakes count as Ocean tiles?
rows.a: No. The Swimmer's Swift Swim, Team Aqua's Submarine Dive and the Scuba Diver's Sunken Treasure only work on Ocean tiles.

rows.q: Do the 4 tiles of the Sky Trainer's Wing Suit have to be in a straight line?
rows.a: No. You may move through any connected tiles as long as your elevation does not increase. Only the first step down uses 1 movement; the 4 tiles after it are free.

rows.q: Can I stop in the middle of a Wing Suit glide and do something else?
rows.a: Yes. The remaining glide tiles stay available for the rest of the turn.

rows.q: Can I act on the tile I travel to with Team Aqua's Submarine Dive or Team Magma's Magma Tunnels?
rows.a: No. You travel as your turn ends, so the turn simply ends there.

rows.q: Can I use Submarine Dive or Magma Tunnels when my turn ends because of a battle? Can I travel to the Distortion World?
rows.a: Yes, you can use them when your turn ends after a battle or after picking up Apricorns. You cannot travel between the Distortion World and the rest of the map.

rows.q: What happens if I walk over a Hidden Spot when moving after a battle with Essentia's Planning Ahead?
rows.a: You pass over it without revealing it. You can only move and end your turn. If you were sent back to your Home Village because you had no usable Pokémon left, you cannot move.

rows.q: How is movement counted along the Worker's Roads?
rows.a: The first step from one Road tile to a connected Road tile uses 1 movement, and every step along the Road after that is free. Stepping onto a Road or off it is counted as usual.

rows.q: How long do Roads last? Do Roads ignore elevation?
rows.a: Roads stay until the end of the game and every trainer can use them. Elevation rules still apply on Roads. No Road is built on the tile where you stood when you turned on Civil Engineer.

rows.q: What if a Hidden Spot revealed with Telekinetic Reach turns out to be an Alpha Pokémon?
rows.a: You must battle it. Your trainer does not move, and the battle takes place on that tile.

rows.q: How are the 2 tiles of Telekinetic Reach counted?
rows.a: As the number of adjacent tiles between you and the target. Elevation and whether you could walk there do not matter. If you Fly from a village at range, you land in the destination village.

rows.q: What if the Ruin Maniac's Artifact Hunter reveals an Alpha Pokémon?
rows.a: The Alpha Pokémon token stays face up on that tile. You do not have to battle it right away, and you are not forced to battle it even if you start a turn on that tile.

rows.q: What if I do not go and collect an Artifact revealed with Artifact Hunter?
rows.a: The Artifact stays face up on that tile and any trainer who reaches it can pick it up. If you collect it, you must give it to one of your Pokémon to hold.

rows.q: Is the Scientist's Field Observation a battle? Can I also do a normal search in the same turn?
rows.a: It is not a battle. It gives no rewards or Apricorns and does not end your turn, and you can still do a normal search in the same turn. The Pokémon card you found returns to the deck.

rows.q: Do I have to reveal the Hidden Spot drawn with the Scuba Diver's Sunken Treasure?
rows.a: No. You may leave it unrevealed.

rows.q: What is in the Hidden Spot discard pile that Sunken Treasure draws from?
rows.a: Apricorn Stashes and Alpha Pokémon tokens that were revealed and discarded. Artifacts, Fallen Stars and Campsites are not included.

rows.q: Can the Gardener's Pick Apricorn and the Kindler's Gather Firewood be used on Apricorn Reefs or Distorted Trees?
rows.a: No. They can only be used on Apricorn Trees.

rows.q: Can Gather Firewood be used on a tree on a tile I am not standing on? Do removed trees come back?
rows.a: You can remove any Apricorn Tree anywhere on the map. Removed trees do not come back for the rest of the game.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Rewards · Other Trainers' Actions
rows.q: Who benefits from the Catch Size Dice?
rows.a: Only the Fisherman. The Catch Size stays attached to the Pokémon wherever it goes, but it only adds health when the Pokémon belongs to a Fisherman who has unlocked Catch of the Day.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Rewards · Other Trainers' Actions
rows.q: What counts as a "wild Pokémon" for the Black Belt's Super Training?
rows.a: Alpha Pokémon, Legendary Pokémon and Gods are included. In a Swarm Battle you gain 2 Journey Points for each Pokémon you defeat.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Rewards · Other Trainers' Actions
rows.q: What if I capture another Bug type during the extra turn from the Bug Catcher's Catching Frenzy?
rows.a: During that extra turn you get neither the Journey Points nor another extra turn. If you capture several Bug types in one battle, you gain 2 Journey Points for each but only one extra turn.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Rewards · Other Trainers' Actions
rows.q: Can the Backpacker's Portable Tent restore a fainted Pokémon?
rows.a: Yes.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Rewards · Other Trainers' Actions
rows.q: What happens to my turn if I am challenged through the Interviewers' Big Scoop?
rows.a: Once that battle is over, the challenged trainer's turn ends.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Rewards · Other Trainers' Actions
rows.q: Can Big Scoop be used when another trainer gains a Journey Stamp outside their own turn?
rows.a: Yes. If it is neither trainer's turn, you just battle and nobody's turn ends. If the other trainer is inside a village, they may decline the challenge.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: Can the Chef's Ingredient Expert be used during a battle?
rows.a: Yes. At any time, you can convert Apricorns one for one into other Apricorns of the same tier.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: Can the Poké Fan's Loyalty Card give me the same Battle Item I just crafted?
rows.a: Yes. You get any one Battle Item of your choice.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: For the Collector's Pokémon Collector, what goes into the stamp rewards move pool?
rows.a: Pokémon you release and learned moves you discard. Pokémon defeated in battle do not.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: How many cards can I add per turn with Pokémon Collector?
rows.a: One per turn.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: In what order are the Dragon Tamer's +5 evolution cost and an effect that halves evolution cost applied?
rows.a: Add the +5 first, then halve the total.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: In what order are the -2 evolution cost from the Lady's Noble Heritage and a half-cost effect applied?
rows.a: Apply the -2 first, then halve. The cost never drops below 0.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: Can the Pokémon Breeder's Egg Move teach the move of the final evolution?
rows.a: No. Only the move of the very next evolution can be taught.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: If I discard the Egg Move, do I lose the Almost Perfect IVs bonus and can the Pokémon evolve again?
rows.a: No. Even after the Egg Move is discarded, the health and initiative bonuses remain and the Pokémon still cannot evolve.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: Do I pay the evolution cost when teaching an Egg Move?
rows.a: Yes. You get it instead of evolving, so the evolution cost is paid as usual.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: Can a Pokémon hold 2 Artifacts with the Backpacker's Holding Capacity?
rows.a: Yes, if they are different Artifacts. Artifacts are Held Items too, so it can also hold one Artifact and one Battle Item.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — Crafting · Stamps · Evolution · Party
rows.q: What happens when a Pokémon holding 2 Held Items is given to another trainer?
rows.a: The second Held Item goes into the receiving trainer's bag. The same applies when Team Rocket steals it.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — When Unlocked: Acolytes · Swapping Cards
rows.q: Can a Diamond, Pearl or Platinum Acolyte add 1 Arceus card to the Follower token's 2 cards to use a Play 3 effect?
rows.a: Yes. The remaining card can be either that God's card or an Arceus card.

rows.sectionTitle: Trainer Cards — When Unlocked: Acolytes · Swapping Cards
rows.q: Does the God obtained through an Acolyte's Red ability earn the "Capture a Legendary" Journey Stamp?
rows.a: No. That stamp is only earned by capturing a Legendary Pokémon yourself.
